authoring_note: Re-authored from pre-fix briefing only (no fix diff). gold=function/module-level root cause without naming fix constructs; wrong=plausible-but-incorrect, different mechanism.

gold.summary: Submitting a JetStream stream create request whose sources list contains a null element crashes the server with a runtime nil pointer panic and a segmentation fault, instead of returning a clean validation error.
gold.root_cause: In the stream module of the server package, the routine that validates a stream configuration walks the list of configured sources and, for each entry, reads fields off that entry (such as its name) to check them. When the incoming request body deserializes a list that includes a null element, the corresponding entry in the sources list is an empty/absent pointer rather than a real source object. The validation routine assumes every entry is present and immediately reads through that pointer without first checking whether it is absent, so dereferencing the empty entry triggers a nil pointer panic and tears down the server rather than rejecting the configuration.
gold.remediation: In the source-validation loop of the stream configuration check, detect an absent/empty source entry before accessing any of its fields and treat it as an invalid configuration, returning a validation error rather than continuing to dereference it.
evidence: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

wrong.summary: Submitting a JetStream stream create request whose sources list contains a null element crashes the server with a runtime nil pointer panic and a segmentation fault, instead of returning a clean validation error.
wrong.root_cause: The crash originates in the request decoding layer rather than in configuration validation. When the JetStream API handler parses the incoming create request body, the JSON unmarshaller is allowed to populate the configuration structure even though the sources list is malformed. Because the decoder does not reject a list element that decodes to a null object, the partially populated structure is then passed downstream in an inconsistent state. The real defect is that the request handler accepts and forwards a structurally invalid payload instead of rejecting it at the boundary, leaving the rest of the server to operate on a half-formed configuration.
wrong.remediation: Harden the JetStream API request handler so that, after decoding the create payload, it verifies the integrity of the decoded sources list and rejects any request that produced a null or malformed element at the parsing boundary, returning an error before the configuration is ever handed to downstream processing.
evidence: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference

wrong_rationale: It is plausible because rejecting malformed input at the decoding boundary is a legitimate defensive pattern and the symptom does involve a deserialized null entry, so an engineer might harden the request handler. It is incorrect because the panic actually occurs later, inside the configuration validation loop that dereferences the empty source entry; fixing only the decoding layer points at the wrong subsystem and leaves the unguarded dereference in the validation routine intact.
